title: The War Named After A Pastry Shop
description:
The Pastry War (1838-1839) is named after a French pastry chef. He complained that Mexican officers looted his shop and demanded 60,000 pesos (Mexican sources say the officers just refused to pay their bills). France later demanded 600,000 pesos for all its citizens' claims, blockaded Mexico's ports and bombarded the fortress at Veracruz. General Santa Anna lost a leg to French cannon fire and had it buried with full military honors. Britain brokered peace and Mexico agreed to pay, but the damages were never paid. In December 1844 a mob dug up Santa Anna's leg and dragged it through the streets.

Sources: Wikipedia, 'Pastry War', 'Battle of Veracruz (1838)', 'Antonio López de Santa Anna'. The looting is dramatised from the chef's account; details such as the year (1828 or 1832) vary by source.
